issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Finish the Editor pilot by moving product UI typography to Geist/Geist Mono in an isolated, reviewable batch, then deleting only legacy style code proven redundant.

In scope

  • Apply Geist to Editor product UI controls, labels, headings, panels, and overlays.
  • Apply Geist Mono only to documented technical values such as coordinates, dimensions, transforms, identifiers, and code/embed snippets.
  • Correct wrapping, truncation, alignment, or overflow exposed by new font metrics without redesigning geometry.
  • Audit and remove legacy UI font declarations, dead selectors, duplicate overrides, and obsolete compatibility rules in the Editor scope.
  • Record before/after CSS metrics and any intentional font-rendering differences.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • The user-content font catalogue, weights, styles, previews, and rendered gallery content must remain unchanged.
  • Prices, dates, body copy, and ordinary labels remain Geist, not Mono.
  • Do not delete a selector without consumer search, build, visual comparison, and state review.

Acceptance criteria

  • Editor product UI consistently uses Geist; Mono usage is limited to approved technical surfaces.
  • All Editor baseline states remain compositionally compatible.
  • Every deletion has evidence that it is unconsumed or redundant.
  • No Bootstrap dependency remains inside the Editor pilot scope.

Dependencies and order

Depends on all Editor foundation, Bootstrap-independence, ownership, and feature migration issues.

Verification

  • Run font/selector/Bootstrap searches, focused tests, and pnpm test:styles.
  • Run the required Angular build.
  • Review desktop/mobile, supported themes, all interaction states, and at least two content fonts.
  • Treat unexplained visual differences as failures.

issues.display_title: Issue #1830: Integrate Countly analytics SDK (production only)
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

The admin app has no product analytics. We cannot answer basic questions: how many people open the editor, how long a session lasts, where users drop off before publishing, or how often the 3D editor throws runtime errors in the field.

Integrate the Countly Web SDK against our self-hosted server, enabled in production only.

In scope

  • Add countly-sdk-web and initialize it from a browser-only app initializer, so SSR never touches the SDK.
  • Environment config: countlyEnabled, countlyUrl, countlyAppKey in all four environment files.
  • Automatic tracking: sessions, pageviews, unhandled JS errors, click heatmap.
  • Pageviews reported as the route config path (/editor/:id), not the resolved URL, so exhibition ids do not explode the Views table into one row per gallery.
  • Identity: merge the pre-login anonymous device id into the account on login (change_id(id, true)), send profile fields via user_details, and reset to a fresh anonymous id on logout so the next visitor on the same browser is not attributed to the previous account.
  • Editor telemetry: emit an editor_action event with { action, exhibition_id } from EditorService.updateLogActivity(), the single sink that ~90 editor call sites already funnel through (publish, save, rename, upload, align, undo/redo, preview mode, transform updates).
  • Export a trackEvent() helper that no-ops on the server and when Countly is disabled, so call sites need no guards of their own.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • Do not add analytics calls to individual editor call sites; hook the existing sink only.
  • Do not enable Countly outside production. Local, dev, and QA ship with countlyEnabled: false and must issue zero network requests.
  • Do not track per-frame or drag-move events; only discrete user actions (pointer-up and explicit commands).
  • No consent/GDPR gating, custom business funnels, feedback widgets, remote config, or A/B testing in this pass.

Acceptance criteria

  • Production build reports sessions, pageviews, errors, and clicks to the configured Countly server.
  • Views table shows /editor/:id as a single aggregated row, not one row per exhibition id.
  • Logging in attaches the prior anonymous session to the account; logging out returns the browser to a fresh anonymous id.
  • Editor actions appear as editor_action events segmented by action and exhibition id.
  • With countlyEnabled: false, no Countly requests are sent and no SDK errors are thrown, including during SSR.

Verification

  • ng build --configuration production and ng build --configuration development succeed.
  • Editor unit tests show no new failures against the pre-change baseline.
  • SSR: the SDK module loads under Node without touching window, and trackEvent() is inert on the server.
  • Manually confirm in the Countly dashboard: session count, /editor/:id view row, an editor_action event, and a user profile after login.

issues.display_title: Issue #1800: [Editor] Fix the Field of View dialog: collapsed layout, stray percentage bubble and footer actions
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

The Field of View dialog (General → Field of View) doesn't hold together as a window.

What you see:

  • The layout collapses — the device list (Desktop / Tablet / Mobile) is supposed to sit beside the preview. Instead the preview drops onto its own line and covers the list, so the three device options are half hidden behind the 3D view. The two halves are sized to add up to the dialog's width exactly, so any rounding pushes them apart.
  • The percentage bubble points at nothing — the reading (e.g. "77%") floats at a fixed spot near the left of the slider whatever value you set, instead of sitting over the handle.
  • The hint text — the sentence about the field of view affecting camera speed is squeezed into the narrow device column at 10px with a decorative bullet, right-aligned against everything else in the dialog.
  • The device list — labels are heading-sized (22px), and selecting one shifts its text sideways because the selected marker is added to the item's box.
  • The preview — square corners, while the dialog and the other editor dialogs are rounded.
  • Cancel / Save — sit inside the scrolling content as small pills, on a different silhouette from the buttons in Edit Frame and Edit Splash Screen, with a large empty gap above them and no divider.
  • Narrow windows — the dialog is a hard 960px, so on a smaller screen it runs past the viewport.

What it should look like

Device list on the left, preview beside it, always. The percentage bubble sits over the slider handle and moves with it. Title and hint on the full dialog width. Cancel and Save in the dialog's own footer, matching the other polished editor dialogs.

Scope

  • Put the device list and the preview on a real grid instead of two fixed widths that fill the dialog exactly; stack them on narrow screens.
  • Bind the percentage bubble's position to the slider value it already prints.
  • Move the title and hint into a header on the full width, and drop the decorative bullet.
  • Device list: label-sized type, minimum 44px rows, and a selected state that doesn't shift the label.
  • Round the preview and give it the dialog's border.
  • Move Cancel and Save into the dialog footer, on the shared editor-dialog button geometry, closed off by one divider.
  • Cap the dialog's width against the viewport.
  • Accessibility: the device options become real buttons (they were javascript:; links), with pressed state, focus rings, and labels on the −/+ steppers.

Verification

  • Open Field of View: the device list sits beside the preview, nothing overlaps.
  • Drag the slider end to end: the bubble tracks the handle at both extremes.
  • Switch Desktop / Tablet / Mobile: the label doesn't jump, and the tablet/mobile frame overlay still fits the preview.
  • Cancel and Save sit in the footer, same size as Edit Frame's, and still save/discard as before.
  • Tab through: device options and steppers take focus with a visible ring.
  • Narrow the browser: the dialog stays inside the viewport and the layout stacks.
  • Check light and dark.
